28                                   AURORA

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>presented itself. For indeed, arsenic can truly not be fixed at all, unless the skilled operator has an equal knowledge of its dyeing spirit <note>original: "spiritū eius tingentem"; referring to the volatile essence responsible for color changes</note>, in which matter indeed all philosophers have slumbered, attempting in vain to achieve anything from it. Whoever, therefore, is ignorant of this spirit, let him have no hope of fixing it, nor of bestowing upon it the power by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. Therefore, I make it known to all that the whitening of which mention was made is derived from a false foundation; by it, copper <note>original: "cuprū"</note> is falsely whitened, not changed. The Sophists <note>Pseudo-alchemists or deceptive practitioners</note> mixed copper <note>original: "venerem"; Venus, the alchemical name for copper</note> masked and disguised in this way with twice its amount of silver <note>original: "lunæ"; Luna, the alchemical name for silver</note>, and sold it to goldsmiths and coin-makers. Finally, indeed, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters—not only those who sold it, but also those who bought it. 

          Some of the sophists took red arsenic <note>likely realgar</note> instead of white, and this itself resulted in a false art. Since in whatever way it is prepared, it shows nothing except whiteness. Some progressed further to common sulfur, which they cooked while it was yellow in vinegar, lye, or very sharp urine, day and night, until it emerged white. Afterward, they raised it from common salt and eggshell lime <note>original: "calce ouorum"</note> and, by means of sublimation <term>sublimation</term> <gloss>the process of heating a substance into vapor so it resets as a solid</gloss>, they cooked and sublimated it, and did this many times. <summary>Paracelsus warns that attempts to "fix" arsenic or sulfur to whiten copper are deceptive practices that result in counterfeit silver rather than true transmutation. He details how these "sophistic" methods fail to remove the combustibility of the materials or achieve a permanent change in the metal.</summary>
<keywords>arsenic, copper, silver, counterfeiters, sulfur, sublimation, sophistry, fixation, transmutation, chemical dyeing</keywords>
